name: F.G.L. Airport Granada-Jaén Airport
before:
Granada's airport, about 15 km west of the city near Chauchina and Santa Fe.

The name causes confusion, so it is worth being clear. Jaén is in the title but the city of Jaén is 100 km to the north, so this is a Granada airport in every practical sense, and a client heading to Jaén has a long drive ahead.

Construction began in 1970 and it opened as Aeropuerto de Granada in 1972. It was renamed in June 2006 after Federico García Lorca, the poet, who was born near the city.
